numerical_failure.observed_behavior: scipy.stats.yeojohnson_llf loses precision and overflows: the original _yeojohnson_llf computed the constant term and took np.log of the variance directly, causing precision loss for data like [10, 10, 10, 9.9] at lmb near -14/-20 and overflow in the log-variance term; the pre-fix code also suppressed RuntimeWarning from np.log when variance was too low by substituting -inf.
numerical_failure.expected_behavior: The log-likelihood should be computed without the constant term (avoiding precision loss) and the log-variance computed in the log domain (avoiding overflow), so the llf curves for data and -data agree under the sign-flipped lmb mapping shown in the reproduction script.
trigger_conditions: data is nearly constant with tiny variance, e.g. data = [10, 10, 10, 9.9]
lmb far from zero, e.g. lmb in [-20, -10]
comparing yeojohnson_llf(lmb, data) against yeojohnson_llf(-lmb, -data) for the same lmb range
all-positive or all-negative data (special-cased in the fix)
abs(lmb) very small relative to eps triggers a separate log1p branch in the fix

input_output_examples.expected_output: not given in passages; should be finite and consistent with yeojohnson_llf(14, -data) under the symmetry shown in the reproduction script

oracle_clues: Reproduction plots llf_pos (yeojohnson_llf(lmb, data)) against llf_neg (yeojohnson_llf(-lmb, -data)) and compares curves
Before/after figures referenced in the PR but not reproduced in the passages
Fix references boxcox_llf as a model for the log-domain computation

numerical_characteristics.precision: rtol=1e-7 in the regression test; the precision-loss case is data=[10,10,10,9.9] with lmb=-14 or 16; eps = xp.finfo(dtype).eps is used as a threshold for abs(lmb) in the fix
numerical_characteristics.magnitude: Overflow case uses lmb=-20 and lmb=20 on the same data; precision loss case uses lmb=-14 and lmb=16; the fix special-cases all-positive or all-negative data (pos = data >= 0) to avoid overflow and precision loss
numerical_characteristics.tolerance: rtol=1e-7 (from test_gh24172 assertions); no separate threshold is stated for separating correct from incorrect answers beyond this relative tolerance
category_specific_evidence: PR #24172 title: fix precision loss and overflow in stats.yeojohnson_llf; references issues #10072 and #19016
Fix removes the constant term to avoid precision loss, valid only for all-positive or all-negative data; mixed data keeps the constant
Discussion: data=[10,10,10,9.9] gives precision loss (no overflow) for yeojohnson_llf(-14, data) and yeojohnson_llf(16, -data)

Test test_gh24172 expects 12.418595783381280 for lmb=-14 and lmb=16 (precision loss), and 12.360966379200528 for lmb=-20 and 12.380287243698629 for lmb=20 (overflow), all with dtype float64 and rtol=1e-7
Expected values were computed with mpmath (mp.dps=100)
Fix casts data to floating dtype via xp_result_type(lmb, data, force_floating=True) and uses xp.finfo(dtype).eps
Numerical instability noted when abs(lmb) or abs(lmb - 2) is very small; the fix has a separate branch for abs(lmb) < eps
Original code suppressed RuntimeWarning when variance is too low, using finfo smallest_normal
reproduction_risks: Mixed-sign data keeps the constant term and is explicitly left alone, so reproductions must not use mixed data to show the fix
Behavior under JAX JIT is uncertain; discussion states it may not work with JAX JIT
Discussion notes other numerical issues may arise when sigma^2 is very small and data is tightly clustered at zero; not resolved
Empty array handling returns NaN and was adjusted for JAX

provenance.value: scipy.stats.yeojohnson_llf loses precision and overflows: the original _yeojohnson_llf computed the constant term and took np.log of the variance directly, causing precision loss for data like [10, 10, 10, 9.9] at lmb near -14/-20 and overflow in the log-variance term; the pre-fix code also suppressed RuntimeWarning from np.log when variance was too low by substituting -inf.

The log-likelihood should be computed without the constant term (avoiding precision loss) and the log-variance computed in the log domain (avoiding overflow), so the llf curves for data and -data agree under the sign-flipped lmb mapping shown in the reproduction script.
